leaves.cannot_prove: Lines outside the excerpts (covered by the full-log survey, not by these unit cases)
leaves.equivalence: The scanner is line-local except for ordering by the docker timestamp prefix, which the excerpts keep byte for byte. Every marker line of the l-e incident (the teardown, the parent-exited line, the 42 broadcast stalls, the orderly stop) is inside the l-e range. The same scanner over the 31 full engine-stream logs of every box fetch on the hub agrees with each run's recorded engine_crashed outcome and adds one new DEAD: l-e. That survey is in the delivery note
leaves.implementation: harness/fixtures/native43_engine_death: verbatim 1-based line ranges, PROVENANCE.json with source and excerpt sha256 (Fixtures re-checks both when the hub fetch is present); the two host-stop-intent.json files are whole copies. Some cases drop named lines (the orderly triggers, the teardown) from an excerpt to build the counterfactual; each case says which
leaves.name: box-log-excerpts
leaves.replaces: The retained host stream engine-stream.log / engine-stream.err of four box incarnations (the host observer's follow of `docker logs --timestamps` of qwen-flash-prod): l-e q18a-native43-lifecycle, native39-trunk, native33, native35 p-c

leaves.cannot_prove: nvidia-smi latency and hang behaviour on the box
leaves.equivalence: The watch reads only the last integer of each row and the exit code. The queue's device sampler (e2_memory_attribution.sample) runs the same query on the box with one more column, and the last-integer rule fits both. A non-zero exit or a timeout counts as an error, never as death (l-e logged an nvidia-smi TimeoutExpired at 11:03:22)
leaves.implementation: A shell script passed as --gpu-cmd that prints "index, MiB" rows: the l-e values 22925/22835/23037/22947 from client-samples.timed.jsonl, one rank at 3 MiB (the l-e post-teardown value), or exit 9
leaves.name: fake-nvidia-smi
leaves.replaces: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used --format=csv,noheader,nounits` on the box CT (the watch's default --gpu-cmd)

leaves.equivalence: The watch reads stdout true/false and the "No such" text of a missing container, which is the docker CLI's own wording; any other failure is an error and is not counted as death
leaves.implementation: A shell script passed as --docker: echo true, echo false, "Error: No such object" on stderr with exit 1, or exit 7
leaves.name: fake-docker-inspect
leaves.replaces: `docker inspect --format {{.State.Running}} qwen-flash-prod` on the box CT (--docker)

leaves.cannot_prove: That each real client exits on SIGTERM. Python's default TERM action terminates, and a TERM-ignoring client is SIGKILLed after the grace (tested)
leaves.equivalence: The watch treats the client as an opaque process: exit code, process group and stdin. The l-e row1 client produced no output and no record before the hub's SIGTERM (qual-row1.log 0 bytes, qual-row1.json absent), which is what the sleeping child shows
leaves.implementation: python3 -c children: sleep 600 (a client blocked on a dead engine), exit 3, ignore SIGTERM, write stdin to a file, touch a readiness marker
leaves.name: client-processes
leaves.replaces: The queue's long engine-facing clients (e3_q18a_qualification.py, e3_q18a_lifecycle.py, PY_HYGIENE)

leaves.cannot_prove: Flush latency of the box observer (a marker reaches the watch one poll after the observer writes it)
leaves.equivalence: The observer appends bytes with os.write in arbitrary chunk sizes. The scanner keeps the partial last line until its newline arrives, and the split-read case decides like the one-shot read with the same running sha256
leaves.implementation: A thread that appends the l-e teardown line after the client is up; a loop that appends the l-e excerpt in 997-byte pieces
leaves.name: growing-log-feeder
leaves.replaces: The host observer (e3_native28_host_observer.Sink) appending docker log bytes to engine-stream.log during the run
